That supports the con central bridge that a coherent beginningless-past alternative remains available. It does not specifically rebut the pro central bridge’s actual-infinite premise or inference, so option-1 is excluded.

bundles.evidenceText: at no point in the infinite past could we find the man counting down
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that completing the beginningless countdown today implies completion at every earlier point, contradicting the hypothesis that the counter was still counting. This directly attacks the con subsidiary bridge preserving the beginningless-countdown alternative. Under direct-attack specificity, option-2’s pro-support recoding is excluded.

bundles.evidenceText: It's enough to have a restricted principle of sufficient reason in a case like this
bundles.rationale: The proposition is that a restricted explanatory principle suffices to demand why an infinite countdown ends now rather than earlier. That independently supports the pro subsidiary bridge that a beginningless countdown cannot be completed. It does not deny the con bridge’s narrower claim about inference from an endless forward count, so option-2 is excluded.

bundles.evidenceText: just seems to me to be no less mysterious
